questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose Tenerife because of it's nicheness. Not a lot of people searched there, so i figured that was ideal for me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different than first anticipated. Very chaotic because of the structure of the university, and as well as the lack of information given by the univiersity. As an Erasmus student at Universidad de La Laguna, we needed to really seek help and information our selves, for us to get just a tiny bit of information.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In the sense of the university's information, it was very sparse. We didn't get a 'tour' in the university's system. People in authority did not really know it either - so overall, very difficult to find the needed information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: not really anything.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: very easy. Just through Facebook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That they need to look in advance, and that they might like to either prioritize living close to campus, or in the respective city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: again, it's about the lack of help and information. Even when teachers were asked, they said that there was not really as procedure for the Erasmus-students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: chaotic, not very sructured

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: we could always go to the secretary's office, but even they found it hard to give us answers, so it often ended up with us going between teachers and the secretary's to pass information to each other.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: again, did not make sense. In the beginning, we apparently had chosen something we figured out we could not have (even tho it was checked by coordinators and other exchage-teams) - so we had to change subjects up to four times, which led to us joining classes 1,5 months later than the other students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would really tell them, that it's super important that you arrive at your destination with your head set to still deal with a lot of administratuve stuff, because the respective host institutions does mostly not have all the requirered information.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: overall was the academic programme okay. A lot of it was well planned, but not very easy to access for the students. With that being said, did it feel like we took a lot of the same courses - the theme, the motive and the goal was the same in the subjects that we were requirered to take.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Although the courses were offered at fourth-semester Bachelor's level, I found the academic level to be lower than at UCPH. In particular, the courses replacing Communication and Dissemination covered topics that I had already completed as part of my Bachelor's programme in Denmark. This meant that some of the content was repetitive and did not provide the expected academic progression.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Compared to UCPH, the teaching style was generally more lecture-based and focused on memorization rather than discussion and critical reflection. I also experienced less structured communication regarding course requirements and examinations, which made it challenging to navigate the semester. However, adapting to a different academic culture was a valuable learning experience that strengthened my flexibility and independence.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: whatever they feel like doing. If they're up for exploring - go see some cool paces around town, if they're exhausted - rest and maybe go to the beach? It's a lot for one to change the daily life like that, so do what feels right. Have a coffee with someone maybe? hahaha

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) It's not gonna get done today, but that's not your fault
2) Be patient 
3) Do not let the admin wear you down

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: it can be a bit chaotic in the Universidad de La Laguna, because they're not used to hosting a lot of exchange students. They're sweet tho!

questions.answer: That i dared to do something so drastic - move abroad for half a year.
